Blender scientific visualization: an evidence-led integration

Private additive review · 17 November 2026

The project has a strong foundation: numerical models, declarative X3D scenes, Blender authoring, independent renderers, a scene corpus and learning loops can correct one another. The most useful next step is a shared contract for what each result establishes. It should connect the existing tools and preserve their different responsibilities.

This pass reads the three supplied files and the actual private branch claude/project-thread-0lc3kd of hagopjay/x3d.ml, pinned at c1634f5c4f29c4220a092510807a430ce4cbfd2e. All three attachments match their branch counterparts byte for byte. The review preserves the original documents and archive, adds structured inventories and corrections, and implements two small integration adapters. It also executes new Blender 5.2.4 precision and Blender 5.3.0 native-splat controls. No remote repository is changed.

What the archive actually contains

The archived expert folder has 439 files totaling 4,583,862 bytes: 217 Python scripts, 126 X3D documents, 74 Markdown files, 13 JSON files, five shell scripts, three PLY files and one patch. Its 27 dependency directories containing only documentation are historical snapshots, not runnable source checkouts.

The raw workflow records 14 slice digests, the original 18 bridge proposals, 36 verifier responses and a critic. The critic contributes nine additional bridges, B19–B27; its tenth suggested entry is a rule-hygiene note. The complete catalog retains 27 bridge IDs and 221 verifier notes, including contradictory claims and the original source lines.

Source rescue has therefore partly happened already. B24 should recover the missing replay material rather than recopy everything: there are no archived PNG, EXR, .blend, SPZ, SOG, VDB or JSONL files in this folder. The 111-item candidate Tier A manifest points to external scenes; it does not contain them. Old PSNR, timing and corpus results remain historical observations unless their specific inputs and output bytes can be recovered or regenerated.

See the kit salvage review, full inventory and raw-workflow summary. All 217 archived Python files parse; static execution leads identify paths, subprocesses and dynamic imports worth reviewing. Parsing is not evidence that a script is safe, portable or scientifically correct. Archived kits were not executed wholesale.

A taxonomy that makes the work reusable

Classify each item along several independent axes. A single project folder or confidence grade cannot express these distinctions.

Axis Useful classes Example
Scientific object Samples, scalar/vector/tensor fields, surfaces, volumes, graphs, trajectories A covariance matrix and its point observations
Representation Raw arrays, scientific projection, scene graph, authoring scene, radiance model, raster figure A VTP point array versus a colored sphere glyph
Activity Compute, encode, transform, import, export, validate, render, inspect, compare, learn Blender save/reopen readback
Acceptance facet Legality, loadability, visibility, completeness, quantities, appearance, dynamics, provenance, resources, rights An XSD pass establishes legality under one schema
Evidence mode Reported, inspected, executed, independently reproduced A retained old JSON result remains reported evidence unless the appropriate operation is rerun
Outcome Pass, fail, partial, unknown, with a stated comparison A successful export that omits points is a completed operation with a retention failure
Operational readiness Archived, recoverable, adaptable, replayable, gated, integrated A script with absent absolute-path inputs is adaptable rather than replayable
Ownership Existing core, consumer adapter, fixture, integration proposal Extend x3dprov; avoid a second provenance protocol

The important architectural shift is to separate an evidence record from the activity it describes. Reading a Cycles receipt today creates a new inspection record; it does not mean Cycles ran today. A version announcement can be checked against primary documentation without an X_ITE renderer. An actual vertex comparison can establish geometry retention while appearance remains untested.

Scientific quantities must survive the display mapping

The reusable scientific record is a quantity with an identity, association, components, units, coordinate frame, missingness and uncertainty assumptions. Color is a declared mapping from that record into a visual channel. Preserve both sides of the mapping.

Research Loom illustrates the distinction well. Its membrane display exaggerates height while the exported VTP retains unexaggerated displacement and velocity. Its ellipsoid is a fitted Gaussian contour, not a generic confidence region for the mean. Its steady ABC flow gives trajectories with periodic seam clipping; a line drawn directly across the box would invent a path segment.

This pattern transfers to molecular confidence, medical-style volume phantoms, geoscience, mechanical simulation and game debugging. A pLDDT color requires proof that the source field actually means pLDDT; an arbitrary experimental PDB B-factor does not acquire that meaning from a palette. A volume needs spacing, orientation and transfer-function records. A gameplay trace needs its time step, force convention and distinction between physical state and presentation effects.

Blender may compute scientific results through Python or Geometry Nodes. The principle is reproducible numerical authority, not a ban on analysis inside an authoring application. Likewise, a mesh is not automatically a measurement and a splat is not automatically useless for measurement: suitability follows from the acquisition, calibration, reconstruction, uncertainty and intended task.

Two precision lessons with actual Blender data

The old phrase “six versus fifteen orders of magnitude” confuses significant precision with exponent range. Precision must be budgeted at the coordinate magnitude used by the actual storage and transform path.

Synthetic metric frame Direct global maximum coordinate error Local storage with binary64 origin restoration
ECEF-like 0.2345000003 m 0.000001890585 m
UTM-like 0.1543210996 m 0.000001890643 m

The probe uses actual Blender 5.2.4 LTS, build cd5dc428cce1, saves and reopens the .blend, reads MeshVertex.co, and compares against an independent struct binary32 reference. Deliberate vertex changes are detected. The source coordinates and reversible origin survive as retained source data.

The origin is added back outside Blender in Python binary64. Moving the object back to a very large Blender world translation can reintroduce precision loss. Centering preserves physical units; rescaling changes the mapping and needs its own explicit conversion. The example does not promise micrometre accuracy for arbitrary scenes or GPUs, and coordinate magnitude does not identify a CRS. Use X3D's existing Geospatial/GeoCoordinate/GeoOrigin direction where applicable.

Native splats: the former future task is now a measured route

Blender 5.3 was released on 10 November 2026. Its primary release notes document native splat imports, attributes and rendering, alongside color and transform limitations. The new control goes further than those release facts: it runs an official Blender 5.3.0, build 02f0899d78e3, whose downloaded archive matches the vendor SHA-256. It imports four deliberately asymmetric SH3 PLY splats.

The measured route distinguishes raw DC radiance from RGB, sigmoid opacity from logits, exponential scale from log scale, normalized quaternion ordering, all 15 higher-order RGB coefficient slots, positions/object transforms and the absence of a per-asset training-color-space flag. The ecosystem fork's native X3D 4.1 export/import is checked as a separate route. Blender's own lack of native splat export is not a statement about that fork's exporter.

The transform control reproduces an important limitation: applying object rotation/scale changes the represented world covariance when the splat's attributes are not transformed consistently. Preserved positions alone would miss this. A Gaussian is its center, covariance, opacity and directional radiance—not simply a point with a radius.

This closes a useful part of B13. It does not establish B01's SH0–SH3 ladder at large sizes, multi-pose image fidelity, SPZ conversion quality, general transform correctness or a supported CI matrix. Those remain separate experiments.

The storage arithmetic also needs a precise layout. SH3 has 59 meaningful model scalars, or 236 bytes at float32. The common reference PLY adds three normal fields, producing 62 float32 values and 248 payload bytes per splat. Header, endianness and declared property types matter. Neither a PLY extension nor a ZSTD container by itself guarantees lossless scientific quantities.

Preserve existing provenance and repair its actual boundary

The private src/x3dprov.py hashes scene content after removing provenance, comments and whitespace-only text, then applies XML canonicalization. Its malformed-XML fallback uses a different text normalization. Research Loom uses exact file-byte hashes and canonical JSON hashes for different purposes. These identifiers must keep their method names; an apparently matching 64-character string is not a universal content identity.

Two integration problems were reproduced:

  1. In _inject_meta, re.sub treated serialized JSON as a replacement template. Escaped newlines, Windows paths and replacement-like strings could be decoded or rejected. An archived xprov copy already contained the correct callback pattern. The proposed core patch adopts that one-line repair, with regression tests. The original archive stays unchanged.
  2. A caller could append to a stale stamped scene and use the previous recorded output as the default input identity, making the extended chain verify. The new figure adapter first refuses stale or broken input. This is an explicit caller precondition; it does not silently change the old protocol's repair semantics for every other consumer.

The figure adapter records link_existing_render, not render. It binds each source packet, selected frame, X3D export, renderer receipt and image to the existing chain. It checks live producer files and decoded geometry. It preserves both the original packet-frame hash and the export-normalized frame hash: normalizing integer/float values or adding defaults can change canonical JSON identity without changing the represented geometry.

A hash chain helps reveal accidental gaps. It is not an authenticated publisher signature or proof that the recorded science is true. Keeping original evidence, live bindings and clearly scoped observations is essential even after a chain verifies.

Ontology hooks with clear implementation boundaries

The supplied JSON-LD inventory uses a local urn:x3d-scivis:inventory: vocabulary. It aligns artifacts, datasets and claims with PROV entities, validation and transformation runs with activities, and bridge categories with SKOS concepts. PROV usage/derivation relations are kept distinct: an evidence file is not an activity merely because it mentions a tool.

Concept Existing hook Required local detail
Artifact / dataset prov:Entity Locator, byte length, hash method, SHA-256, confidentiality
Validation / transformation prov:Activity Input/output identities, exact tool build, scope, time, outcome
Derivation prov:wasDerivedFrom Which representation changed and which quantities were retained
Scientific observation SOSA alignment hook Observed property, procedure, feature of interest and result; do not label every render an observation
Quantity QUDT alignment hook Unit URI where known, numeric value, association and uncertainty
Bridge / category skos:Concept Stable B-ID, broader/narrower concepts and related work package
Loss Local comparison record Field, coordinate convention, expected projection, tolerance and observed difference
Claim Local scoped assertion Subject, facet, evidence mode, outcome, supporting artifacts and freshness

The JSON schema and Python checks enforce the inventory contract. The Turtle hooks, SHACL shapes and SPARQL example make external graph integration concrete. SHACL checks metadata structure; live byte checks and facet-support queries remain separate. Neither stage infers physical truth. Rights are source assertions and policy inputs, not legal conclusions inferred from a filename or short regex.

For a future domain record, require at least: quantity ID, name, association, components, units, coordinate-frame ID, missingness, numeric range, uncertainty description, display transfer function and a comparison profile. A profile should state its equivalence relation. Quaternion comparison must allow q and −q; Gaussian comparison should include covariance under a basis change; SH comparisons need the declared coefficient basis and rotation convention.

Sequence the remaining work by what it resolves

First: freeze reusable baselines. Preserve the current stock/fork point-line fixture, native 5.3 splat probe, precision control and the original broken provenance behavior. Recover the absent images and corpus files by exact identity where available; regeneration creates a new run. Reconcile B09's 11-versus-12 rule list before treating it as a standard gate.

Next: close one ordinary exchange loop. B27's points, ColorRGBA and lines, B26's GLB cross-check and B04's value/default tests share most of their machinery. Use the existing Research Loom readback fixture and preserve scientific arrays in sidecars/VTP. Fix omissions in the owning exporter, then compare the same before/after values. Keep native pixels, geometry and source data as separate acceptance criteria.

Then: the splat ladder. Reuse the recovered synthetic generators, but name fixture cardinality, float layout and exact values. Measure opacity in both alpha and logit spaces where clamps matter. Test SH0–SH3, asymmetric covariances, multiple camera poses and declared transforms. Parser limits, XSD limits and renderer ordering are different failure modes. A resource refusal should remain distinguishable from an invalid scene. Increasing parser allowances alone is not a complete large-file strategy.

Extend to scientific domains with independent answers. B19 should begin with an analytic anisotropic-spacing volume phantom. B20 should preserve atom and residue identities in a tiny molecular fixture before adding large structures. B22 should compare keyed values at fixed fractions and individual ROUTE endpoints, rather than counting tags. B23 should check joint hierarchy, centers and weight normalization. B21 can extend the new origin fixture into a declared CRS path.

Orchestrate after interfaces stabilize. B14 needs import-safe local commands and a durable checkpoint test that survives a process kill. Wrapping an old script that runs remote commands at import is not a neutral node. The inventory adapter is deliberately read-only and does not become a new workflow engine. Any future post-export validator also remains distinct from the process boundary that limits a Blender script's filesystem or network effects.

Evaluate models last. B18 needs an actual feasible prompt selector, held-out split, fixed budget and paired protocol. The old “115 feasible prompts” is not present as a reproducible selector. Report legality, visible output and fidelity with their own denominators; first-try-valid rates are not scientific-fidelity rates. B15 should use a vector of independent oracle findings, including unknown or failed execution states, rather than hide disagreement in one average.

Working heuristics

  1. Select a representation for a question; do not infer its scientific authority from its file extension or visual polish.
  2. Preserve the smallest input that can refute a claimed property. Four distinct splats can expose ordering mistakes; they cannot establish million-splat scale.
  3. Compare actual output data. Retained metadata can describe geometry that was silently omitted or changed.
  4. Record expected projections as well as losses. A glyph mesh is a deliberate representation change; losing the observation coordinates is a different event.
  5. Freeze a before-fix case before changing a converter. Regression evidence requires the same contract on both sides.
  6. Upgrade only the claim that was tested. A native import, a source inspection and a multi-pose renderer comparison have different coverage.
  7. Keep known failure results. An Apply Transform counterexample is valuable evidence and a regression target, even though the probe itself passes.
  8. A derived figure should retain its numerical source, display mapping, selected state and renderer record. Its beauty does not substitute for any of them.
  9. Promote a new rule after a minimal reproducer and a held-out check; matching the mutants used to write a rule is coverage, not generalization.
  10. Prefer one owned implementation with many adapters. A shared identity and loss vocabulary will compound more effectively than parallel scorekeepers.

The long-term payoff is an expanding collection of small, inspectable scientific cases. Each new domain supplies a useful figure and a new way to detect a wrong one. Each repaired bridge increases how many tools can carry the same question without losing its meaning.

Bridge audit

Scientific visualization bridges: evidence review and consolidation

Private working analysis, 17 November 2026. This subtask read the complete three attached files. It did not access the private repository, recover its kits or rerun the historical 52-agent workflow. The machine-readable bridge-catalog.json preserves the original source locations, grades, input paths, criteria and verifier objections for all 18 bridges, and adds the nine critic candidates as proposals. Its hashes identify the exact attachments. The companion current-evidence-map.json compares actual retained Research Loom bytes with these proposals; it does not turn historical numbers into new measurements.

The strongest idea survives review: use numerical data, declarative scenes, authoring tools and independent readback as cooperating instruments. The main weakness is the reuse of a single confidence label for an entire bridge. One bridge can contain an inspected implementation, an unretained timing, a planned patch and an unrun acceptance criterion. Those are four different claims.

What to retain, correct and combine

Retain the separation between schema legality, visible output, completeness and scientific fidelity. Preserve the source-scene loss audit before export, the known-answer fixture factory, the renderer-independent splat oracle, explicit per-field tolerances and the insistence on exact version identities. These are reusable across STEM, mathematics, molecular rendering, heritage and gameplay.

Correct the impression that the bridges are largely ready-made wrappers. The document itself records hard-coded scratch paths, missing fixture packs, conflicting commit pins, unrun pass criteria and import-time remote calls. The work is primarily interface definition, evidence recovery and scope control. That is worthwhile engineering; disguising it as wiring would conceal the important work.

Combine overlapping ledgers instead of building new ones for each domain. B10 supplies scientific cases; B11 supplies corpus selection; B04/B06/B27 supply value and appearance tests; B12 supplies provenance; B05/B14 supply workflow adapters. They should share identities and findings while retaining their different responsibilities.

This consolidation keeps the original bridge IDs as durable references. It changes their implementation boundaries: a module has one owner, while many bridges can use it. Cross-repository proposals should carry the public-safe fixture and code only; private survey text, corpus IDs, raw model outputs and internal owner notes remain separate.

Ordering that avoids duplicated work

Start with B24, even though it appeared near the end of the original catalog. The earliest useful result is a recoverable baseline, not another headline benchmark. Source files described in a document are not recovered artifacts. Recover the exact bytes, record hashes, classify executable side effects and make old result files read-only inputs to the review. Recreated output must be labelled as a new run.

Then finish the smallest reusable contract: one scientific fixture, one source packet, explicit scientific-to-display mappings, named export projections, readback findings and an actual output receipt. Research Loom already provides this pattern for three non-splat studies. Extend it with one ordinary point/line regression and one asymmetric precision/origin case before expanding the corpus.

Keep B02 and B03 as coordinated alternatives for different failure modes. An honest resource-limited validator verdict remains useful even when partitioned exports avoid a parser limit. A larger parser allowance does not prove the XSD engine can validate every large attribute. Byte budgets should be per actual encoding and field, with a measured refusal outcome.

Do not block small-scene work on B02. B05's guard prototypes used small exports, and B09's scientific probes can run independently of huge-splat support. Likewise, B10 fixture authoring and B06 baseline capture can begin before B04 importer repairs. Only an acceptance criterion that expects repaired values depends on the repair. The catalog records hard, conditional and removed dependencies separately.

After values and representation are stable, run larger corpus tiers and native splat/codec paths. Workflow orchestration comes after stable command contracts. Model benchmarks come after a pre-registered selector, a held-out split, calibrated oracles and a defined budget. A stub workflow can be useful much earlier, as long as its stubbed stages are explicit.

Taxonomy: classify by meaning and failure mechanism

Use multiple orthogonal facets instead of one deep folder tree.

Facet Suggested values Why it matters
Scientific role observation, model parameter, derived quantity, uncertainty, assumption Distinguishes a measured point from an authored glyph radius
Representation raw array, mesh, centerline, point glyph, volume, splat, semantic graph A useful display representation need not preserve analytical operations
Transformation solver, resampling, coordinate change, projection, quantization, authoring, rendering Makes losses attributable to a particular operation
Data space physical/model coordinates, display coordinates, world coordinates, linear RGB, encoded RGB, opacity, logit Prevents an error bound being quoted in the wrong space
Gate syntax, schema, semantic rule, model witness, numerical reference, retention, render, rights policy Prevents an XSD pass from becoming a scientific claim
Evidence status described, recovered, inspected, executed, reproduced, superseded, unavailable Records what was actually done rather than inferred from a grade
Failure mechanism omitted, reordered, quantized, remapped, stale, truncated, resource-limited, unsupported, assumption-violated Gives repair tools a concrete target
Scope fixture, bounded subset, corpus partition, declared profile, arbitrary file Blocks narrow-fixture results from being generalized silently
Rights explicit grant, restricted, absent, conflicting, unresolved Keeps legal facts separate from a versioned eligibility decision

Domain tags can then connect structural biology, volumes, geoscience, dynamics, acoustics, heritage, game mechanics and mathematics without duplicating the same color/precision/provenance rule in every domain folder.

Ontology hooks to add, without inventing a second ontology

The following are proposed modeling hooks. Use a small local vocabulary for new scientific concepts and align existing standards when their precise versions are chosen. Namespace labels here are design references, not evidence that those schemas or validators have been implemented.

ValidationAttempt exact candidate, profile, instrument, result, refusal reason SHACL report alignment for graph constraints; XSD metadata for XML
RetentionMeasurement source field, destination field, numeric space, error, tolerance Local exchange contract and measurement vocabulary
RenderConfiguration renderer/build, camera, lighting, display transform, sampling Provenance activity plus local camera/color/sampling terms
Figure case/state, render derivation, image bytes/pixel hash method Provenance entity; explicit raster/EXR sidecar asset relation
RightsAssertion asserted licence, source, evidence date, uncertainty dct:license, rights-holder attribution; versioned policy separately
FailureFamily minimal reproducer, causal category, held-out membership Local QA taxonomy, links to rules and affected capabilities
BridgeProposal owner, inputs, scope, dependencies, maturity, adoption status Local planning ontology; links to implemented activities rather than becoming one

The useful graph joins are concrete: a failing retention measurement points to the source field, the export activity and the destination representation; the fixture that discovered it links to the corrected rule; a later run uses that rule and cites the fixture without claiming that the discovery set is held out. Legal-parent ontology lookups establish graph legality, while numeric witnesses establish different claims about coordinates, weights and quantities.

Heuristics worth institutionalizing

  1. The unit of confirmation is a scoped claim. A bridge, repository or application does not receive a blanket confidence upgrade.
  2. Keep the data authority explicit. Unexaggerated arrays and quantities remain authoritative when an attractive mesh is stretched, colored or lit.
  3. Read the thing that could be wrong. Metadata identity checks cannot detect a changed Blender vertex; retained geometry metadata cannot stand in for decoded coordinates; an exported render cannot prove a legend.
  4. Compare in the declared space. Quaternion sign, logit/alpha conversion, linear/encoded color and global/local coordinates each need their own metric.
  5. Expected loss is a contract, not an excuse. A declared projection can pass while losing unsupported semantics, but its label must prevent reuse as a complete scientific round trip.
  6. A refusal is information. Unsupported data, a resource cap and a validator exception should be distinguishable from invalid science.
  7. Freeze before fixing. Baseline and repaired results must share fixtures, scope and instruments apart from the intended change.
  8. Use cheap exact checks first. Counts, coordinate transforms, arrays, topology, units and known-answer fields precede image judges and model calls.
  9. Oracle disagreement is a result. Record which semantics differ; do not reduce validation, drawing and data fidelity to a single average score.
  10. Derivation is not authenticity. Hashes identify bytes and chains record relationships; signatures and authenticated provenance are separate layers.
  11. Schema-valid output can launder lost input. Validate input, audit source capabilities, compare output meaning and retain every refusal/loss.
  12. Workflow simplicity is a research feature. Thin local wrappers and durable identities make failures inspectable before an agent graph is added.

Future experimental program

The first pack should contain ordinary point/line geometry, an asymmetric tetrahedron, a known color ramp with a legend, a large-origin/small-offset coordinate case, one SH0/SH3 splat pair and an explicitly failing control for each gate. It should use one manifest and one findings vocabulary, while each consumer declares its own supported subset. Current Research Loom supplies the first two categories and a tested data/geometry/render separation; the remainder requires actual fixtures.

The next domain packs are an anisotropic volume phantom (B19), a tiny molecule with stable identities (B20), a CRS/local-origin terrain sample (B21), fixed- fraction animation (B22) and an HAnim hierarchy/skin control (B23). Domain meaning must be testable before presentation detail is increased. A pLDDT ramp must be tied to a prediction source; a generic crystallographic B factor should not be silently reinterpreted as pLDDT.

Only after those contracts exist should B18 compare authoring lanes. Select feasible prompts by explicit capabilities, use matched tasks and budgets, keep held-out material separate, report valid/draws/complete/retained/data-correct stages independently, and calibrate presentation order for any judge panel. The original estimated cost and old percentage baselines do not authorize or justify a new online experiment.

The five historical user questions are now actionable defaults rather than reasons to stop local work: keep exact per-run validator identities; preserve recoverable evidence privately; refresh the native-splat capability probe; offer named appearance/comparison profiles; and prepare reviewable patch kits for owning repositories without sending them. The private access and source availability question remains material because several high-value kits may exist only in the named branch. That gap should be stated precisely, with the attached summaries still used as a backlog and evidence map.

Reproduce the aggregate software/metadata check

With the original Research Loom distribution and private repository checkout:

python3 -m pip install -r requirements-review.txt
python3 verify_review.py \
  --study /path/to/x3d.STEM/studies/research-loom \
  --private-repo /path/to/x3d.ml
python3 ontology/check_graph.py

Pass --python313 /path/to/python3.13 to repeat the stdlib inventory suite in that interpreter. The individual Blender commands are in the probe reports. Rebuilding scientific data, changing tools or editing a bound file requires a new inspection and, where relevant, a new producer run.

What the raw 52-agent result establishes

The 651,632-byte JSON has 14 reader digests, a catalog of 18 bridges, 18 verified bridge rows containing 36 verifier verdicts, and a critic with 11 missing-link items, 19 overclaim items and ten suggested entries. Nine suggested entries are the real B19–B27 bridges; the tenth is a rule-hygiene note.

The reported 52-agent arithmetic is consistent with 14 readers + one synthesizer + 36 verifier reports + one critic. The JSON stores their texts; it does not include provider execution receipts or proof that those reports were independent executions. Its lower historical grades are 13 Likely, four Suspected and one Confirmed. These remain source-reported grades, not fresh confirmations made by this audit. In particular, a verifier's ok: true can coexist with numerous problems and a downgrade.

The raw workflow is valuable as a research log and structured hypothesis bank. It should not be used directly as a green capability registry. Preserve each critic correction alongside the original pass criterion instead of extracting only the synthesizer's headline numbers.

Portability findings from static inspection

All 217 Python files parse under the audit interpreter; this is syntax inspection, not a compatibility or execution claim. Forty-five distinct absolute path literals point principally to October scratch and /mnt/project-files layouts. Many scripts create files, reset Blender state, parse CLI arguments or dynamically load dependencies at module scope. Importing them as orchestration nodes can therefore execute a whole experiment or fail before a node has been called.

The scanner labels candidate operations with their line numbers and whether they occur syntactically outside a function. This includes code inside if __name__ == '__main__' and other conditional blocks, so that flag is a review lead rather than proof of import-time execution. The scan found 11 process-launch call sites, ten dynamic-code/import call sites and two direct network candidates. These are expected ingredients in experimental scripts; they explain why adaptation must precede execution. Examples include eval of data fields in kits/compression/splatfid/{abl,fid}.py, module-level exec_module in Blender probes, CLI parsing in guard phases, ffmpeg subprocesses in never_black.py, a curl fetch in fetch_hanim.py, and networked texture loading in the archived importer.

There are 27 documentation-only dependency directories resembling add-on, validator or renderer checkouts. They contain README/contribution/release-note files without executable source. Their names are historical context, not a dependency lock. The one complete patched_src prototype is a separate case.

A concrete provenance defect worth carrying forward

src/x3dprov.py is byte-identical to kits/x3d-ml/x3dprov.py, SHA-256 74746444c0093a72636686fa325da5950802d860861e61a859ed1c0ba78cedae. The alternative kits/x3d-ml/xprov/x3dprov.py has SHA-256 922d45c1ede366b634247d26c1a4de23c007460b83e09603cd9f3583936de661. Besides documentation, the second copy contains a meaningful callback change:

# src: replacement text interprets regex backslash escapes
re.sub(r"</head>", metas + "</head>", xml, count=1)

# archived variant: callback inserts JSON-bearing metadata literally
re.sub(r"</head>", lambda match: metas + "</head>", xml, count=1)

x3dprov-escape-microreproducer.json records a fresh standard-library reproduction of that replacement-expression behavior, without importing the old module. A valid JSON detail containing a newline and a Windows path is corrupted by the replacement-string operation; the callback preserves its JSON semantics. This supports a small regression test and private fix proposal to the existing provenance owner. It does not establish that every x3dprov path has been tested. The useful correction was already latent in the archive.

Keep four identities distinct when integrating figure chains: original file bytes, parsed/canonical X3D content, scientific arrays, and decoded pixels. They intentionally answer different questions. The existing v0.1 source removes comments/provenance/whitespace-only text before C14N, with a textual fallback for malformed XML. It has no explicit hash_method field or external assets[] binding. An adapter should declare these conventions and derive from the existing record rather than treating all SHA-256 values as interchangeable.

Practical next sequence

  1. Adopt the hash inventory and mark the missing payload classes explicitly. Preserve the three original knowledge documents and the raw workflow.
  2. Reuse Research Loom's current mixed geometry, source/hash binding and measured Blender/GLB readback as a small working core. They advance parts of B04/B10/B11/B12/B26/B27; they do not validate the old entire corpus or splat color/oracle ladder.
  3. Add the escaped-metadata regression, point/line retention fixture, current large-coordinate probe and a fresh SH0–SH3 ladder with field-level losses.
  4. Resolve exact upstream sources and recover missing renderer image pairs; only then establish cross-engine pixel tolerances and a before/after ledger.
  5. Attach a thin checkpointed workflow to the existing scorekeeper/provenance owner. Preserve capability facets and refusals instead of reducing all checks to one "confirmed" badge.

The durable product of this pass is an archive map and an adoption route. It does not execute networked historical kits, spend on models, contact other owners, mutate public repositories or replace the existing evidence protocol.

K01 · runtime freshness

Blender 5.3.0 was released on 10 November 2026. Blender 5.2.4 is the current 5.2 LTS patch on that date. Keep the 5.2 LTS and 5.3 native-splat lanes separately pinned.

Evidence: primary_documentation_checked. S01, S02

K02 · native splat attribute order

Blender stores raw SH degree-zero coefficients in radiance:base.xyz, followed by activated opacity in w. The new four-splat native 5.3 test reproduces this mapping and all 15 higher-degree RGB coefficient slots.

Evidence: primary_documentation_and_executed_native53_control. S03

Next action: Keep asymmetric known-answer splats. Treat SH basis, channel order, opacity activation and scale activation as separate declared mappings.

Native import and rendering are available in Blender 5.3; the official notes state that native export is absent. The new structural test reproduces native PLY import, a fork X3D 4.1 round trip and a loss of covariance under Apply Transform.

Evidence: primary_documentation_and_executed_native53_control. S03

Next action: Keep native import, fork export, rendering and transform preservation as separate capabilities. This four-splat structural test does not complete the B01 renderer or scale ladder.

Ontology hooks: ImportRoute, ExportRoute, KnownLimitation.

K04 · splat byte arithmetic

SH degree 3 uses 59 model scalars, or 236 bytes at float32. The common reference PLY adds three normal scalars, yielding 62 float32 properties and 248 bytes per vertex, before the header.

Evidence: derived_from_primary_code. S05

Next action: Name the property list, scalar width, endianness and header separately. Preserve the 68/104/164/248-byte table only for this declared layout.

This distinction concerns significant precision, not exponent range. Reopened Blender 5.2.4 mesh coordinates matched float32 quantization in two metric coordinate controls. Local-origin storage substantially reduced the measured errors.

Evidence: executed_bounded_control. S06, S07

Next action: Retain 64-bit source coordinates and reversible origin/units metadata. Budget absolute error at the actual coordinate magnitude.

Standard avoids an additional creative view transform, but display conversion, material lighting, exposure and alpha still affect pixels. X_ITE exposes colorSpace, displayColorSpace and toneMapping controls.

X3D has named FloatVertexAttribute and matrix vertex attributes for shaders, plus typed Metadata. These carriers do not automatically provide scientific meaning or an equivalent of a Geometry Nodes graph.

Reproduced precision control

Blender 5.2.4 LTS, build cd5dc428cce1, saved and reopened real mesh data. Readback matched an independent binary32 packing reference. Source coordinates and a decimal origin remained in the saved source text. Deliberate actual-vertex changes were detected with the source metadata left unchanged.

Synthetic metric frame Direct global maximum error Restored local-origin maximum error
ecef_like 0.2345 m 1.89058483e-06 m
utm_like 0.1543211 m 1.89064303e-06 m

Restoration happens in Python binary64 outside Blender world transforms. Translating an object back to a large float32 world position can reintroduce the loss. This is a bounded storage result, not a GPU, X3D or general geospatial-accuracy certification.

Native Blender 5.3 results

Native Blender 5.3: seven splat questions, measured

Private research result · 17 November 2026.

The recovered seven-question probe is now an executed, bounded structural test. Four asymmetric splats with all SH coefficients through degree 3 import into an actual Blender 5.3.0 native Gaussian-splat PointCloud. The current ecosystem fork exports them to X3D 4.1 and imports them back with identical native attribute values. A separate XML comparison checks the declared scientific mapping rather than trusting the fork's own parser. Applying an object transform does not preserve the splats' world covariance in the tested control.

This supplies a concrete B13 result. It does not complete the B01 size ladder, renderer parity experiment or large-corpus round-trip programme.

Answers from actual imported attributes

The expected values derive from the written PLY property list and exactly serialized float32 inputs. The tested fork is not used as the import oracle.

Question Observed answer Maximum absolute difference
Q1: Is radiance:base.xyz raw DC or reconstructed RGB? Raw SH DC coefficients. The reconstructed-RGB hypothesis fails distinctly. DC: 0; RGB hypothesis: 1.9358104
Q2: Is radiance:base.w activated opacity? Matches the sigmoid of the PLY opacity logit. 4.9436317 × 10⁻⁸
Q3: Is scale linear? Matches exp(scale_i) from the PLY log-scale fields. 1.4238989 × 10⁻⁸
Q4: What is the quaternion ordering? Normalized (w,x,y,z) in Blender's native attribute. 4.7503028 × 10⁻⁸
Q5: How are higher SH slots ordered? All 15 radiance:sh_i RGB triples match channel-major PLY f_rest unpacking, with i = degree² − 1 + coefficient. 0 across every tested slot
Q6: What happens to the PLY coordinates? The default importer leaves these raw positions unchanged, with an identity object matrix; world positions match the source. Raw and world positions: 0
Q7: Is a color-space label exposed? No dedicated encoding label was found by the inspected PointCloud RNA/custom-property checks. color_attributes exists as a collection. Descriptive inspection; no color-fidelity conclusion

Q6 reports numeric behavior for this import operation. It does not establish the physical meaning of an arbitrary PLY's axes. Keep the source up/forward convention explicit. Q7 is bounded introspection, not proof that every internal Blender color mechanism lacks metadata.

Fork transfer and independent checks

The probe selects only the original native object and uses matching identity-axis export/import settings. Its independent XML reader checks 20 arrays: positions, scales, orientations, opacities, the DC term and all 15 higher SH coefficient triples. This catches a mapping error even if a fork importer and exporter accidentally agree with each other.

The informational diagnostics concern unused DEF names and the absence of an authored Viewpoint. The XML artifact is a structural transfer fixture, without an authored publication camera. No native X_ITE rendering was executed here.

Apply Transform: a demonstrated limitation

The control copies the native object, applies translation (1,2,3), Euler rotation (0.2,−0.3,0.4) radians and scale (1.5,0.75,2), then calls the actual Blender Apply Transform operator.

Before and after the operation, world covariance is reconstructed from the actual scale/quaternion attributes and object matrix:

[ \Sigma_{world}=M R\,\mathrm{diag}(s_x^2,s_y^2,s_z^2)R^T M^T. ]

World positions change by at most 4.7683716 × 10⁻⁷ fixture units, while world covariance changes by as much as 0.22836776 fixture units². Position preservation alone would therefore miss the shape change. The report records both raw attribute snapshots and both covariance arrays.

Keep object transforms explicit until a route proves preservation of the full Gaussian, including directional SH behavior. This probe does not implement a general affine covariance decomposition or Wigner-D SH rotation.

/path/to/blender --background --factory-startup --threads 2 --python-exit-code 1 \

Evidence data model

Data model and inference boundaries

The inventory is an adapter over existing evidence. It has no universal “Confirmed” field and no ranking that collapses scientific validity, software execution and image quality into one number.

Entity Necessary role Suggested ontology alignment Boundary
Claim A statement with named subjects, facets and scope terms A claim/proposition entity in the owning ontology; lineage may use PROV-O A title is not evidence
EvidenceRecord A recorded observation with method state and outcome PROV-O entity; qualify measurement-style observations with SOSA where appropriate A recorded pass is not a fresh execution
Artifact Exact retained bytes and a relative source-root locator PROV-O entity A byte hash is not publisher authentication
ToolBuild Version, source artifacts and recorded runtime details PROV-O entity for the build; connect an executing software agent separately A build is not automatically an agent
ValidationRun A recorded or absent execution PROV-O activity not_run cannot support an executed claim
Bridge Historical B01–B27 integration identifier SKOS concept for catalog alignment Method overlap does not complete a bridge
Transformation An explicit coordinate/encoding operation PROV-O activity when an actual operation is recorded A matrix declaration alone does not establish its execution
Loss A measured or declared loss with an explicit scope SOSA observation for measured quantities; otherwise a loss assertion Semantic loss and numeric error need different descriptions
Dataset Numeric/model observations behind a representation Dataset entity in the owning ontology Display coordinates may have been magnified
CoordinateFrame Handedness, axes and unit policy A domain coordinate reference entity; QUDT unit links when identified Axis conversion, origin shift and rescaling are different operations

These are proposed hooks, not blanket OWL equivalences. The owning ontology can add stronger class axioms after checking the representation's intended domains and ranges. In particular, globally mapping every artifacts field to prov:used would infer that receipt entities are activities. This adapter uses scivis:boundArtifact and leaves activity-specific PROV qualification to the owning ontology.

Worked geometry query

The tensor transfer record has subject tensor-correlated, facets geometry.coordinates, geometry.topology, geometry.color_attributes, and scope terms selecting the authored case, saved frame4 and owned geometry subset. A claim requiring those same terms can cite it after current artifact and producer binding inspection passes.

The record cannot support any of these different statements:

  • a different membrane or imported CSV case survived;
  • every frame survived Blender editing;
  • a modifier graph or material graph survived;
  • X_ITE and Cycles produced equal pixels;
  • the source observations are Gaussian;
  • an edited geometry file still satisfies the original physical model.

They fail by different subject, different scope, or missing facet. Lineage through prov:wasDerivedFrom does not change that result.

Three color observations

The owned .blend transfer measures scientific color attributes through an explicit sRGB/linear conversion. The GLB receipt separately measures serialized FLOAT colors and Blender's BYTE_COLOR reimport quantization. The authored PNG then adds illumination, transparency, shading and a display transform. These are three different observation levels. Exact color attributes can coexist with quite different rendered pixels.

Current binding and original execution

The bank source map includes ../../lib/stemkit/core.py; the release source map alone does not. Import reads both maps and resolves their references within the repository root. Evidence has separately checked artifacts and source_bindings, so an unchanged receipt with an edited producer source does not silently describe the new code.

An inspection snapshots hashes at a time. It neither freezes the filesystem nor prevents files changing afterwards. Support output records the inspection time, and the inventory digest prevents accidentally applying one inventory's inspection to another inventory. Before a consequential new statement, inspect the current files again and rerun whichever domain instrument its facet needs.

Historical counts and present denominators

The flywheel source uses corpus counts with several denominators and explicitly records disagreements. The imported text fragments are reported and retain that uncertainty. Reading and hashing that document establishes that the fragments are present, not that the old corpus exists now or has the same membership. A fresh corpus count needs an explicit manifest, included/excluded rules, a census command, and a retained result from that command.

Privacy follows the evidence

Every imported node is private. This graph is unsuitable for direct publication because its source locators and historical assertions expose private project structure. A future public projection should enumerate approved fields and artifacts, remove private locators and assertions, then validate the projected graph separately. Removing a title or replacing a private repository name alone would not sanitize nested measurements or recorded command output.

One-oracle convergence exercise

Converge on one known-answer fixture before adding more agents

The existing work has several complementary witnesses. The useful next step is to send one small asymmetric scientific fixture through them while retaining independent questions at every boundary.

Fixture

Reuse the Research Loom mixed fixture as the geometric seed: an asymmetric tetrahedron, a sampled line and a point set, with distinct colors, opacity, group identifiers, scientific scalar values, units and a nonzero origin. Add explicit ColorRGBA and unlit variants as separate candidates. Keep the original Float64 scientific packet, its stable IDs and known-answer values beside every projection. Do not turn the new variants into claimed executed results merely by adding them to a catalog.

One invariant sheet should state:

  1. exact record and point counts, coordinates and connectivity;
  2. the right-handed frame, proper Y-up/Z-up rotation and reversible origin;
  3. scientific values, units, color mapping and missing-value conventions;
  4. the supported projection for each hub and its expected losses;
  5. which parts of the picture are authored appearance.

Use existing tools for the question each can answer

Gate Existing instrument Keep the answer narrow

Structural validity Pinned x3d_mcp schema and semantic adapter Named schema/version and implemented semantic checks
Actual scene values Owned X3D/VTK readers Coordinates, topology, arrays, units and grouping that the projection promises

The inventory joins those original records. It does not become another validator or figure-signing system.

Baseline, intervention, comparison

Freeze the pre-fix source commits, fixture bytes and per-route loss ledger. Choose one repair, such as ordinary PointSet export in the ecosystem fork. Rerun the same invariant sheet and both the matching positive fixture and a deliberate incorrect twin. Compare the affected counts and attributes; leave unaffected dimensions unclaimed. Only then add the corresponding bridge completion evidence to its owning catalog.

For appearance parity, use a separate unlit color chart and recorded camera, lighting, alpha compositing, background and display settings. Pixel difference is meaningful only after those choices are aligned. Record failed pairs as useful evidence rather than choosing whichever renderer mode produces the best score for each row.

For the splat branch, the new four-splat SH3 probe establishes a bounded native attribute-layout observation. The old N/SH/opacity/scale ladder remains its own experiment. Extend the common invariant sheet with explicit log/linear scale, logit/alpha, quaternion order, SH basis/channel ordering, axis transform and numeric tolerances. Do not extrapolate a small raw-data test to pixels, a 65k/1M-splat limit, or arbitrary transformed covariance.

Acceptance record

A useful completed comparison has original inputs, exact tool builds, raw results, expected and observed losses, the scope of each facet, and one mutation that its oracle rejects. The bridge map then points at that evidence. There is no need to collapse all facets into a single pass percentage.

Independent review and resolution

Independent integration review

Read-only review of the figure-link adapter, its tests, the one-line private x3dprov repair and tests, the evidence inventory adapter and its delivered support queries. No bound source, receipt or graph file was edited by this review. In-memory controls were run with bytecode writes disabled.

Must address: noncanonical existing provenance can bypass append refusal

The initial append_verified() implementation accepts both no-record and verified from the legacy protocol. read_steps() recognizes a deliberately narrow textual serialization, requiring name before content. Well-formed XML permits attributes in either order.

A fresh in-memory control performed these steps:

  1. Stamp the adapter test's owned Box fixture with the existing protocol.
  2. Change the existing step meta to <meta content="…" name="x3dprov.step.1"/>.
  3. Change the Box from 1 2 3 to 1 2 4.
  4. Call the initial append_verified() with a new operation.

The legacy verifier reports no-record before append. The initial adapter accepts it, returns a verified one-step chain, and the resulting XML contains two x3dprov.step.1 meta elements: an invisible old record and a new record. Thus the guard's broad claim to refuse stale or broken existing input requires one more structural check.

Recommended narrow fix: an unstamped initialization may contain no x3dprov.* head metadata; if any such metadata exists, require a verified, recognized record and compare parsed step markers to the protocol's recognized step list. Reject unsupported serialization and duplicate/unknown markers rather than treating them as a fresh scene. A paired reordered-attribute control is valuable. This concerns the reusable append API; the three current links start from genuinely unstamped owned exports, so the finding does not by itself invalidate their already delivered geometry/image bindings.

The finding and reproducer were sent to the parent for correction before final packaging. This note records the reviewed initial state; consult the final adapter tests and source identity for its resolution.

Nonblocking future invariant: reproduction must retain structured scope

inventory.validate() requires a reproduced EvidenceRecord to reference a different recorded run with matching subjects and contained facets. It does not currently compare scope_terms between the original and reproduced records. A future record could label a new saved frame as a reproduction of a different frame while sharing the same Dataset and geometry facet.

The delivered inventory does not use the reproduced state, so this is a future schema/policy improvement rather than a false current support result. Require the repeated scope to match, or explicitly model the relation as a new scoped execution instead of reproduction. Independent provenance or operator identity would be a separate stronger policy; different run IDs alone do not establish experimental independence.

Checks that look correct

  • The private core repair uses a replacement callback, preserving JSON newline, Windows-path and regex-like backslash sequences. It reuses the known archived correction without changing the protocol's hash method or public behavior. The five regression tests exercise literal data and repeated chain append.
  • The adapter keeps the original packet-frame canonical hash separate from the exchange-normalized frame hash. Render receipts bind to the former; exported X3D metadata binds to the latter. The sidecar names both methods separately.
  • XML content hash, exact file SHA-256, decoded scientific frame identity and PNG identity have distinct fields. Retrospective render linkage is explicitly render_reexecuted: false; it does not pretend to be a new rendering run.
  • Bound artifact paths are resolved and constrained to explicit roots. Current local bytes and producer sources are checked independently.
  • Support queries apply explicit subjects, facets and structured scope terms. Reading a prior passing receipt retains its recorded execution state while the inspection reports fresh_execution: false.
  • All 23 delivered Claim queries were inspected against the delivered inspection. Six native-browser/post-edit-science controls and the historical corpus-count control remain unsupported; the 16 scoped recorded claims are supported. No geometry claim leaked into pixel parity or new scientific certification in those queries.

The inspected graph contains 238 Artifact nodes, 27 Bridge nodes, 27 EvidenceRecords, 26 ValidationRuns, 23 Claims, 18 ToolBuilds, 12 Datasets, 12 Losses, two CoordinateFrames and one Transformation. These counts describe the inventory structure, not a count of newly reproduced experiments.

Resolution in this delivery

The owning pass addressed both findings before packaging. The figure adapter compares parsed XML provenance markers with the legacy reader and refuses reordered, unknown or misplaced records; eight adapter tests pass. Its append helper is restricted to linking unchanged scene content. The inventory validator now requires matching structured scope terms for a reproduced record; the additional different-frame control raises the suite to thirteen tests. Original archived sources remain unchanged; the separate core callback repair is proposed as a private patch.

Existing provenance adapter

Existing x3dprov figure linkage

This adapter reuses the private x3dprov/0.1 protocol. The vendored module is pinned to private commit c1634f5c4f29c4220a092510807a430ce4cbfd2e plus a one-line literal-replacement callback repair. Its original SHA, fixed SHA and provenance are in vendor/ORIGIN.json. The repair follows the already archived xprov copy; the original archived kits are unchanged.

python3 -m pip install lxml
python3 adapters/x3dprov_link.py --study /path/to/x3d.STEM/studies/research-loom --output private/figure-links
python3 -m unittest discover -s adapters/tests
python3 -O -m unittest discover -s adapters/tests

The selected cases are the three retained Research Loom hero frames. The adapter checks source producer files, exact packet/frame bytes, decoded geometry, actual image bytes and renderer-source identities. It records link_existing_render and explicitly reports render_reexecuted: false. Original files are untouched. Output is a linked X3D document and a sidecar for each case.

There are three distinct identities: file bytes; the original packet frame's canonical JSON; and the exchange-normalized frame's canonical JSON. The existing x3dprov XML-content hash is a fourth method. All retain separate field names. The adapter admits only well-formed owned XML and refuses the protocol's text fallback branch, stale input and broken chains.

The core patch fixes escaped JSON in re.sub replacement text. Five regression cases cover newlines, Windows paths, replacement-like strings, control escapes and Unicode/markup. Before the fix, four cases fail; after it all five pass. The adapter's eight additional controls exercise stale-input refusal, marker location, reordered XML attributes and protocol compatibility. The owned append operation only links unchanged scene content; it is not a general transform API. This remains an unsigned continuity record, not authentication.

A smaller unit of compounding knowledge
